1.9.2.  Combination of Formation Damage and Partial Completion
The pseudo skin presented by Brons and Marting allows for the effect of flow 
convergence on the drawdown.  It is now necessary to assess the combined effects 
of formation damage and partial penetration.  One possible situation is illustrated 
in Figure 52. where the damaged zone is assumed to be very thin and the flow lines 
are parallel within it; flow convergence has taken place deeper in the formation in 
unaltered medium so illustrated.  Note that the problem of vertical flow convergence 
in real wells can be complicated by the effect of perforations not cleaning up as shown 
in Figure 53.;  this aspect will be treated in detail later.  The first step in analysing

Equation 3.26 shows that a positive value of skin factor will indicate that the permeability 
around the well has been reduced (by some form of formation damage). The absolute 
value reflects the contrast between the skin zone permeability and the unaltered zone 
permeability and the depth to which the damage extends into the formation. Part of the 
essential information from a well test is the degree of formation damage (skin factor) 
around a well caused by the drilling and completion activities. Alternatively, a well 
may have a negative skin factor, i.e. the permeability of the skin zone may be higher 
than that of the unaltered zone, caused by the creation of highly conductive fractures 
or channels in the rock. The extent of the damage zone cannot be predicted accurately 
and there may be variations vertically in the extent of the damage zone therefore this 
simple model may not characterise the near wellbore permeability exactly.
An altered zone near a particular well affects only the pressure near that well, i.e. the 
pressure in the unaltered formation away from the well is not affected by the existence 
of the altered zone around the well.

initial_answer:
제한된 perforation entry가 있는 정에서 Horner 직선의 apparent skin을 곧바로 지층 손상 skin으로 읽는 것은 잘못된 접근입니다. 이는 Horner 직선의 apparent skin이 지층 손상 skin뿐만 아니라, **부분 완성( partial completion)**으로 인한 skin 효과도 포함하기 때문입니다. 

KB5에 따르면, apparent skin은 지층 손상 skin(sd)과 부분 완성으로 인한 skin(sp)의 합으로 표현됩니다:  
$$ s = s_d + s_p $$  
따라서, apparent skin을 단순히 지층 손상 skin으로 해석하면, 부분 완성으로 인한 skin 효과를 고려하지 않아 오류가 발생합니다 [KB5]. 

따라서, apparent skin을 지층 손상 skin으로 단정하기 전에는, perforation entry의 영향을 고려해야 합니다.
